verdict.rationale: Requesty supports user-configured policies that act automatically on request-level events. Fallback Policies retry with the next model in a chain when a request fails (timeout, rate limit, error). Per-key spend caps and guardrail content scans are also documented, but the docs only state that caps exist and that guardrails scan content; they do not say what action fires when either triggers. These are fixed gateway behaviors, not a general rule engine where users define arbitrary triggers and actions. Missing for 10: general-purpose event→action rule definitions, webhooks or notifications on events (e.g., spend thresholds, errors), documented actions when caps or guardrails trigger, custom action types beyond routing, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
